v0.0.3.5 (2026-11-15) [testing]
- The tracker window now has a close button in its header, placed beside the status pill, and the redundant outer scrollbar is gone. The job list keeps its own scrolling for narrow windows. Tracking, settings, commands and refresh behaviour are unchanged.

v0.0.3.4 (2026-11-15) [testing]
- The tracker window shows job progress, inventory projections and completion state in a responsive card-based layout: a custom header without the native title bar, summary and job-progress cards, job rows that adapt to the window width, and a persistent footer with the live state. v0.0.3.3 (2026-11-14) [testing]

{"Author":"daemitus, MidoriKami, dajoey","Name":"Lazy WT Math","Punchline":"FFXIV Wondrous Tails probability calculator.","Description":"Adds row probabilities to the Wondrous Tails display along with the average probability of what would happen if you shuffled. Upgraded for modern FFXIV.","InternalName":"LazyWTMath","AssemblyVersion":"3.2.3.8","Changelog":"v3.2.3.13 (2026-11-24) [testing]
- Refreshed the bundled native-window toolkit (KamiToolKit) to the upstream code reorganization, which regroups the toolkit's types into Core, UI and Services namespaces.
- No setting or window behavior changes; the probability overlay builds through the same nodes as before.

v3.2.3.12 (2026-11-23) [testing]
- Refreshed the bundled native-window toolkit (KamiToolKit) to the upstream interface rework, which splits node capabilities into dedicated interfaces (attachable, colour, position, rotation, scale, size, visibility, silent set) and adds a window frame node.
- No setting or window behavior changes; the probability overlay builds through the same nodes as before.

v3.2.3.11 (2026-11-22) [testing]
- Refreshed the bundled native-window toolkit (KamiToolKit) to the upstream layout-engine rework, which rebuilds the internals of the list, grid and tab layout nodes and adds a shared layout base class (LayoutNodeBase) plus size-change batching on the node base.
- No setting or window behavior changes; the probability overlay renders through the same text and collision nodes as before.

v3.2.3.10 (2026-11-21) [testing]
- Refreshed the bundled native-window toolkit (KamiToolKit) to the upstream api16-era release, which reorganizes how native game windows and nodes are built.
- The probability overlay keeps its journal-matched background, text colours, font size and spacing through the toolkit's new node layout.

v3.2.3.9 (2026-11-16) [testing]
- Fixed a crash risk while logging in or out with the Wondrous Tails journal open.
- The probability overlay no longer recomputes every frame.

v3.2.3.8 (2026-11-15) [testing]
- The window was polished for the real in-game font and scale: text no longer clips or sits against card borders.
- Cards keep their content height, so the sticker map, Shuffle average, About and Journal overlay no longer stretch into empty space at large sizes.
- At the default size the whole sticker map is visible in the Idle, Empty and Failed states too, and the three line-chance cards stay in one row down to the narrowest width.
- The header has a bordered name chip, a neutral status pill showing only the state word and a What's new button.

e8f691d: Merge pull request #816 from SlashNephy/feat/alic-hunt-journeys

feat(AetheryteLinkInChat): prefer Faloop's starting points for hunt spawn points
74b4951: feat(AetheryteLinkInChat): add exits missing from the game's map markers

The game's map markers do not describe the exit from Yanxia to the
Doman Enclave (The One River): the marker in Yanxia points to the
obsolete map 437, and the current map 463 has no marker back to Yanxia.
So routes through the Doman Enclave were never considered, which is the
Yanxia example in #656.

- Add MapConnections for such exits, starting with Yanxia <-> the Doman
  Enclave. Comparing Faloop's boundary starting points with the game's
  map markers found no other missing exit
- Consider them in the route calculation as ConnectionTeleportPath,
  without counting the distance inside the connected map, as where the
  exit leads to is not known
- Show them like zone boundaries, and stop the Lifestream teleport there

Refs #656

Co-Authored-By: Claude Mythos 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
a3c0a1f: feat(AetheryteLinkInChat): prefer Faloop's starting points for hunt spawn points

Straight-line distance on the map ignores terrain, height and walls, so
the nearest aetheryte is often not the best one to start from.

Faloop's zone data has the spawn points of hunt marks, each with a
journeyPoiId that points to the aetheryte or zone boundary to start
from. Embed them (generated by Scripts/generate_hunt_journeys.py) and,
when a map link is at a known spawn point, only consider the routes that
enter the map at its starting point. Otherwise, fall back to the
straight-line distance as before.

Refs #656

97ddbb9: Merge pull request #815 from SlashNephy/fix/alic-detect-world

fix(AetheryteLinkInChat): prefer the world name after the cross world icon
e5d9e91: fix(AetheryteLinkInChat): prefer the world name after the cross world icon

DetectWorld picked the first public world in World sheet order whose
name appeared anywhere in the message. Mob names such as Odin and
Behemoth are also world names, so "Odin <map link> <CrossWorld>Cerberus"
resolved to Odin (row 66) instead of Cerberus (row 80), while
"Odin ... Omega" happened to work because Omega is row 39. The map link
trimming only removes text from the link marker (U+E0BB), so the mob
name before the link was kept.

- Prefer the world name right after the cross world icon, or the cross
  world character typed as text
- Otherwise use the world name that appears last in the message

47500d7: fix(FaloopIntegration): log the whole spawn_location payload

Passing the nullable ZonePoiId alone as the params argument of the log
call made it a null array when the value was null (CS8604). Log the

Co-Authored-By: Claude Mythos 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
3cf9a9e: fix(FaloopIntegration): reconnect with a new client after disconnection

After "transport close", SocketIOClient's own reconnection kept the
engine.io session alive (pings continued) but the plugin never received
mob reports again until it was disabled and enabled.

Handle reconnection in the plugin instead, mirroring what re-enabling
the plugin does:

- Disable SocketIOClient's reconnection
- Run a connection loop that logs in again and connects with a new
  Socket.IO client on every disconnection, with exponential backoff
  from 5 seconds up to 5 minutes
- Time out a connection attempt that the server never accepts, since
  ConnectAsync only times out at the transport level
- Stop retrying when the credentials are rejected
- Ignore events from clients that have already been replaced

Refs #687

3cf9a9e: fix(FaloopIntegration): reconnect with a new client after disconnection

After "transport close", SocketIOClient's own reconnection kept the
engine.io session alive (pings continued) but the plugin never received
mob reports again until it was disabled and enabled.

Handle reconnection in the plugin instead, mirroring what re-enabling
the plugin does:

- Disable SocketIOClient's reconnection
- Run a connection loop that logs in again and connects with a new
  Socket.IO client on every disconnection, with exponential backoff
  from 5 seconds up to 5 minutes
- Time out a connection attempt that the server never accepts, since
  ConnectAsync only times out at the transport level
- Stop retrying when the credentials are rejected
- Ignore events from clients that have already been replaced

Refs #687

e8f691d: Merge pull request #816 from SlashNephy/feat/alic-hunt-journeys

feat(AetheryteLinkInChat): prefer Faloop's starting points for hunt spawn points
74b4951: feat(AetheryteLinkInChat): add exits missing from the game's map markers

The game's map markers do not describe the exit from Yanxia to the
Doman Enclave (The One River): the marker in Yanxia points to the
obsolete map 437, and the current map 463 has no marker back to Yanxia.
So routes through the Doman Enclave were never considered, which is the
Yanxia example in #656.

- Add MapConnections for such exits, starting with Yanxia <-> the Doman
  Enclave. Comparing Faloop's boundary starting points with the game's
  map markers found no other missing exit
- Consider them in the route calculation as ConnectionTeleportPath,
  without counting the distance inside the connected map, as where the
  exit leads to is not known
- Show them like zone boundaries, and stop the Lifestream teleport there

Refs #656

Co-Authored-By: Claude Mythos 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
a3c0a1f: feat(AetheryteLinkInChat): prefer Faloop's starting points for hunt spawn points

Straight-line distance on the map ignores terrain, height and walls, so
the nearest aetheryte is often not the best one to start from.

Faloop's zone data has the spawn points of hunt marks, each with a
journeyPoiId that points to the aetheryte or zone boundary to start
from. Embed them (generated by Scripts/generate_hunt_journeys.py) and,
when a map link is at a known spawn point, only consider the routes that
enter the map at its starting point. Otherwise, fall back to the
straight-line distance as before.

Refs #656

Co-Authored-By: Claude Mythos 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
97ddbb9: Merge pull request #815 from SlashNephy/fix/alic-detect-world

fix(AetheryteLinkInChat): prefer the world name after the cross world icon
e5d9e91: fix(AetheryteLinkInChat): prefer the world name after the cross world icon

DetectWorld picked the first public world in World sheet order whose
name appeared anywhere in the message. Mob names such as Odin and
Behemoth are also world names, so "Odin <map link> <CrossWorld>Cerberus"
resolved to Odin (row 66) instead of Cerberus (row 80), while
"Odin ... Omega" happened to work because Omega is row 39. The map link
trimming only removes text from the link marker (U+E0BB), so the mob
name before the link was kept.

- Prefer the world name right after the cross world icon, or the cross
  world character typed as text
- Otherwise use the world name that appears last in the message

{"Author":"The Combat Reborn Team","Name":"Rotation Solver Reborn","InternalName":"RotationSolver","Description":"Analyses combat information every frame and finds the best action.

This means almost all the information available in one frame in combat, including the status of all players in the party, the status of any hostile targets, skill cooldowns, the MP and HP of characters, the location of characters, casting status of the hostile target, combo, combat duration, player level, etc.

e8f691d: Merge pull request #816 from SlashNephy/feat/alic-hunt-journeys

feat(AetheryteLinkInChat): prefer Faloop's starting points for hunt spawn points
74b4951: feat(AetheryteLinkInChat): add exits missing from the game's map markers

The game's map markers do not describe the exit from Yanxia to the
Doman Enclave (The One River): the marker in Yanxia points to the
obsolete map 437, and the current map 463 has no marker back to Yanxia.
So routes through the Doman Enclave were never considered, which is the
Yanxia example in #656.

- Add MapConnections for such exits, starting with Yanxia <-> the Doman
  Enclave. Comparing Faloop's boundary starting points with the game's
  map markers found no other missing exit
- Consider them in the route calculation as ConnectionTeleportPath,
  without counting the distance inside the connected map, as where the
  exit leads to is not known
- Show them like zone boundaries, and stop the Lifestream teleport there

Refs #656

Co-Authored-By: Claude Mythos 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
a3c0a1f: feat(AetheryteLinkInChat): prefer Faloop's starting points for hunt spawn points

Straight-line distance on the map ignores terrain, height and walls, so
the nearest aetheryte is often not the best one to start from.

Faloop's zone data has the spawn points of hunt marks, each with a
journeyPoiId that points to the aetheryte or zone boundary to start
from. Embed them (generated by Scripts/generate_hunt_journeys.py) and,
when a map link is at a known spawn point, only consider the routes that
enter the map at its starting point. Otherwise, fall back to the
straight-line distance as before.

Refs #656

97ddbb9: Merge pull request #815 from SlashNephy/fix/alic-detect-world

fix(AetheryteLinkInChat): prefer the world name after the cross world icon
e5d9e91: fix(AetheryteLinkInChat): prefer the world name after the cross world icon

DetectWorld picked the first public world in World sheet order whose
name appeared anywhere in the message. Mob names such as Odin and
Behemoth are also world names, so "Odin <map link> <CrossWorld>Cerberus"
resolved to Odin (row 66) instead of Cerberus (row 80), while
"Odin ... Omega" happened to work because Omega is row 39. The map link
trimming only removes text from the link marker (U+E0BB), so the mob
name before the link was kept.

- Prefer the world name right after the cross world icon, or the cross
  world character typed as text
- Otherwise use the world name that appears last in the message

Close #661

fix(FaloopIntegration): reconnect with a new client after disconnection
47500d7: fix(FaloopIntegration): log the whole spawn_location payload

Passing the nullable ZonePoiId alone as the params argument of the log
call made it a null array when the value was null (CS8604). Log the
whole payload instead, as the spawn case does.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Mythos 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
3cf9a9e: fix(FaloopIntegration): reconnect with a new client after disconnection

After "transport close", SocketIOClient's own reconnection kept the
engine.io session alive (pings continued) but the plugin never received
mob reports again until it was disabled and enabled.

Handle reconnection in the plugin instead, mirroring what re-enabling
the plugin does:

- Disable SocketIOClient's reconnection
- Run a connection loop that logs in again and connects with a new
  Socket.IO client on every disconnection, with exponential backoff
  from 5 seconds up to 5 minutes
- Time out a connection attempt that the server never accepts, since
  ConnectAsync only times out at the transport level
- Stop retrying when the credentials are rejected
- Ignore events from clients that have already been replaced

Refs #687

{"Author":"Valenth Siveria","Name":"I Am Ready","Punchline":"Automatically accept or decline Duty Finder ready checks based on a configurable counter.","Description":"# I Am Ready

**I Am Ready** is a Dalamud plugin for Final Fantasy XIV that automatically accepts or declines Party and Alliance Ready Checks based on a customizable counter. 

Whether you are stepping away for a moment or just tired of clicking, this plugin handles ready checks for you while mimicking human reaction times.

## ✨ Features

* **Auto-Answer Ready Checks:** Automatically clicks "Yes" or "No" when a ready check appears.
* **Configurable "Yes" Counter:** Set a specific number of times you want to automatically answer "Yes". Once that limit is reached, the plugin will automatically start answering "No" to prevent pulling when you are actually away.
* **Natural Delay:** Enable a randomized delay (0.7 to 2.5 seconds) before the plugin answers, making it look like a natural human reaction.
* **Smart Chat Triggers (Regex):** Add custom text phrases to the plugin. If someone says one of these phrases in Party or Alliance chat (e.g., "reset", "pulling"), your counter will automatically reset back to zero.
* **Bilingual Support:** The user interface is available in both English and German.

## 🚀 Usage

1. Type `/iar` in the in-game chat to open the configuration window.
2. Click the **Inactive/Active** button at the top to turn the auto-responder on or off.
3. Adjust the **Yes Count** slider. For example, if set to `5`, the plugin will answer "Yes" to the next 5 ready checks, and "No" to any checks after that.
4. Click the **Start** button at any time to manually reset your current counter back to zero.

### Chat Triggers (Regex Patterns)
At the bottom of the window, you can expand the **Regex Patterns** section. Here you can add simple words or complex regex patterns. 
If the plugin reads a matching message in your Party or Cross-World Party chat, it will instantly reset your counter to zero, assuming a new pull or instance is starting!

fix(AetheryteLinkInChat): detect own messages by the sender name

Co-Authored-By: Claude Mythos 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
51f1e26: fix(AetheryteLinkInChat): detect own messages by the sender name

SourceKind is only set for battle logs and system messages, so the option
to skip own messages had no effect on player chat such as Say or Shout.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Mythos 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
e8f691d: Merge pull request #816 from SlashNephy/feat/alic-hunt-journeys

feat(AetheryteLinkInChat): prefer Faloop's starting points for hunt spawn points
74b4951: feat(AetheryteLinkInChat): add exits missing from the game's map markers

The game's map markers do not describe the exit from Yanxia to the
Doman Enclave (The One River): the marker in Yanxia points to the
obsolete map 437, and the current map 463 has no marker back to Yanxia.
So routes through the Doman Enclave were never considered, which is the
Yanxia example in #656.

- Add MapConnections for such exits, starting with Yanxia <-> the Doman
  Enclave. Comparing Faloop's boundary starting points with the game's
  map markers found no other missing exit
- Consider them in the route calculation as ConnectionTeleportPath,
  without counting the distance inside the connected map, as where the
  exit leads to is not known
- Show them like zone boundaries, and stop the Lifestream teleport there

Refs #656

Co-Authored-By: Claude Mythos 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
a3c0a1f: feat(AetheryteLinkInChat): prefer Faloop's starting points for hunt spawn points

Straight-line distance on the map ignores terrain, height and walls, so
the nearest aetheryte is often not the best one to start from.

Faloop's zone data has the spawn points of hunt marks, each with a
journeyPoiId that points to the aetheryte or zone boundary to start
from. Embed them (generated by Scripts/generate_hunt_journeys.py) and,
when a map link is at a known spawn point, only consider the routes that
enter the map at its starting point. Otherwise, fall back to the
straight-line distance as before.

Refs #656

Co-Authored-By: Claude Mythos 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
97ddbb9: Merge pull request #815 from SlashNephy/fix/alic-detect-world

fix(AetheryteLinkInChat): prefer the world name after the cross world icon
e5d9e91: fix(AetheryteLinkInChat): prefer the world name after the cross world icon

DetectWorld picked the first public world in World sheet order whose
name appeared anywhere in the message. Mob names such as Odin and
Behemoth are also world names, so "Odin <map link> <CrossWorld>Cerberus"
resolved to Odin (row 66) instead of Cerberus (row 80), while
"Odin ... Omega" happened to work because Omega is row 39. The map link

3cf9a9e: fix(FaloopIntegration): reconnect with a new client after disconnection

After "transport close", SocketIOClient's own reconnection kept the
engine.io session alive (pings continued) but the plugin never received
mob reports again until it was disabled and enabled.

Handle reconnection in the plugin instead, mirroring what re-enabling
the plugin does:

- Disable SocketIOClient's reconnection

  from 5 seconds up to 5 minutes

  ConnectAsync only times out at the transport level

journeyPoiId that points to the aetheryte or zone boundary to start
from. Embed them (generated by Scripts/generate_hunt_journeys.py) and,

enter the map at its starting point. Otherwise, fall back to the
straight-line distance as before.

74b4951: feat(AetheryteLinkInChat): add exits missing from the game's map markers

The game's map markers do not describe the exit from Yanxia to the
Doman Enclave (The One River): the marker in Yanxia points to the
obsolete map 437, and the current map 463 has no marker back to Yanxia.
So routes through the Doman Enclave were never considered, which is the
Yanxia example in #656.

- Add MapConnections for such exits, starting with Yanxia <-> the Doman
  Enclave. Comparing Faloop's boundary starting points with the game's
  map markers found no other missing exit

  without counting the distance inside the connected map, as where the
  exit leads to is not known

a3c0a1f: feat(AetheryteLinkInChat): prefer Faloop's starting points for hunt spawn points

Straight-line distance on the map ignores terrain, height and walls, so
the nearest aetheryte is often not the best one to start from.

Faloop's zone data has the spawn points of hunt marks, each with a
journeyPoiId that points to the aetheryte or zone boundary to start
from. Embed them (generated by Scripts/generate_hunt_journeys.py) and,
when a map link is at a known spawn point, only consider the routes that
enter the map at its starting point. Otherwise, fall back to the
straight-line distance as before.

Refs #656

e5d9e91: fix(AetheryteLinkInChat): prefer the world name after the cross world icon

DetectWorld picked the first public world in World sheet order whose
name appeared anywhere in the message. Mob names such as Odin and
Behemoth are also world names, so "Odin <map link> <CrossWorld>Cerberus"
resolved to Odin (row 66) instead of Cerberus (row 80), while
"Odin ... Omega" happened to work because Omega is row 39. The map link
trimming only removes text from the link marker (U+E0BB), so the mob
name before the link was kept.

- Prefer the world name right after the cross world icon, or the cross
  world character typed as text
- Otherwise use the world name that appears last in the message

Close #661

3cf9a9e: fix(FaloopIntegration): reconnect with a new client after disconnection

After "transport close", SocketIOClient's own reconnection kept the
engine.io session alive (pings continued) but the plugin never received
mob reports again until it was disabled and enabled.

Handle reconnection in the plugin instead, mirroring what re-enabling
the plugin does:

- Disable SocketIOClient's reconnection
- Run a connection loop that logs in again and connects with a new
  Socket.IO client on every disconnection, with exponential backoff
  from 5 seconds up to 5 minutes
- Time out a connection attempt that the server never accepts, since
  ConnectAsync only times out at the transport level
- Stop retrying when the credentials are rejected
- Ignore events from clients that have already been replaced

Refs #687

{"Author":"Valenth Siveria","Name":"I Am Ready","Punchline":"Automatically accept or decline Duty Finder ready checks based on a configurable counter.","Description":"# I Am Ready

**I Am Ready** is a Dalamud plugin for Final Fantasy XIV that automatically accepts or declines Party and Alliance Ready Checks based on a customizable counter. 

Whether you are stepping away for a moment or just tired of clicking, this plugin handles ready checks for you while mimicking human reaction times.

## ✨ Features

* **Auto-Answer Ready Checks:** Automatically clicks "Yes" or "No" when a ready check appears.
* **Configurable "Yes" Counter:** Set a specific number of times you want to automatically answer "Yes". Once that limit is reached, the plugin will automatically start answering "No" to prevent pulling when you are actually away.
* **Natural Delay:** Enable a randomized delay (0.7 to 2.5 seconds) before the plugin answers, making it look like a natural human reaction.
* **Smart Chat Triggers (Regex):** Add custom text phrases to the plugin. If someone says one of these phrases in Party or Alliance chat (e.g., "reset", "pulling"), your counter will automatically reset back to zero.
* **Bilingual Support:** The user interface is available in both English and German.

## 🚀 Usage

1. Type `/iar` in the in-game chat to open the configuration window.
2. Click the **Inactive/Active** button at the top to turn the auto-responder on or off.
3. Adjust the **Yes Count** slider. For example, if set to `5`, the plugin will answer "Yes" to the next 5 ready checks, and "No" to any checks after that.
4. Click the **Start** button at any time to manually reset your current counter back to zero.

### Chat Triggers (Regex Patterns)
At the bottom of the window, you can expand the **Regex Patterns** section. Here you can add simple words or complex regex patterns. 
If the plugin reads a matching message in your Party or Cross-World Party chat, it will instantly reset your counter to zero, assuming a new pull or instance is starting!
